ca_found_in_the_duffle_crag.blurb: A small roadside crag in the Hidden Valley part of Joshua Tree National Park, set among the Roadside Rocks formations on the west side of the park road, a little right of and in front of its neighbour Lost In The Shuffle Crag. Thirteen trad routes are split fairly evenly between a northeast face and a southwest face, mostly following slanting cracks. Grades run from the easy fives into the low 5.10s, with a single 5.12 outlier, so it suits moderate climbers who want a short walk from the car. Expect quality to be modest compared with the park's famous walls; it works as a quick warm-up or an add-on stop.

ca_k_rock.blurb: A low-key outcrop in Apple Valley in the high desert, sitting just south of the Horsemen's Center sport crags and visible from Highway 18. It mixes about nine boulder problems with a handful of short trad lines. The bouldering is mostly easy, from the very easiest grades up to V1, with a lone V3 as the standout, and the trad routes are all around 5.9. Faces are slabby, so technique and footwork count for more than strength. It tends to be quiet, and late fall through early spring is the comfortable window. Bring a pad or two, since slab falls can be awkward.

ca_ah_boulder_the.blurb: A large boulder in the campground area of Idyllwild County Park, in the San Jacinto Mountains above the town of Idyllwild. It has thirteen problems spread over every side, from slabby faces to overhanging walls, with a cracked east face visible near the entrance trail. Most problems sit in the V0 to V2 range, with a handful of easier warm-ups and a couple of much harder lines at the top end. A short walk from the park entrance gets you there. The park's boulders are often lightly visited, so you may well have the place to yourself.

ca_alanis_morrisette_wall.blurb: A modest trad wall in Joshua Tree National Park's Lost Horse area, tucked on the rock behind the busy Atlantis Wall at about 4,100 feet. About a dozen routes, nearly all gear-protected and a few set up for top-roping, run from fourth-class scrambling through the easy and moderate fives, topping out at one 5.10. The climbing is decent rather than outstanding, which makes it a sensible fallback when the neighbouring wall is crowded, and a good pick for beginners learning to place gear. Reach it by parking where the public road ends and hiking a trail east toward the Atlantis formations.

ca_buckthorn_boulder.blurb: A small alpine boulder at roughly 8,000 feet in the San Bernardino Mountains near Big Bear Lake, in the Snow Summit boulder cluster. Thirteen problems face south, east and west, almost all at the very bottom of the grade scale, from V-easy to V0, with knobby faces and a few thin cracks. The stone carries a lot of lichen, though the south side is cleaner. It lies a short scramble from the neighbouring Skyline Boulder, and the walk in from the parking area takes about a minute, so it suits beginners and families. Watch for the dense buckthorn brush below the south side.

ca_grand_canyon_of_the_tuolumne.blurb: A remote canyon climbing zone in Yosemite's Tuolumne Meadows backcountry, stretching downriver from Glen Aulin. This is committing terrain reached by a long trail walk, and the routes are mostly traditional multi-pitch lines on domes and walls. Of thirteen routes here, all but one are free climbs, running from the 5.8 range up to 5.12, with the hardest grade the most common; one is an aid line. The history is patchy, old bolts and pins turn up, and route information is thin, so expect to route-find and judge fixed gear for yourself. It is a place for experienced parties comfortable with wilderness logistics.

ca_crippler_boulder_the.blurb: The best-known boulder at The Dreamers, a small bouldering zone on the Sherwin Plateau above the Owens River Gorge near Mammoth Lakes, at about 7,100 feet. Thirteen problems on pocketed tuff run from V0 to V6, with several in the V3 to V6 range. The south and west sides are steep, fingery pocket pulling, while the east side is a slab holding the easier lines. It is the first boulder on the right as you walk in from the parking spot. At that elevation spring and fall are the best seasons, since summer gets hot.

ca_circle_crag.blurb: A small south-facing bowl of rock in the Indian Cove amphitheatre of Joshua Tree National Park, between the group and family camping loops at about 3,200 feet. Most of its thirteen routes are short trad lines of around thirty feet, with two sport routes and one top-rope problem. Grades spread from an easy 5.3 up through the 5.6 to 5.8 range where most of the climbing sits, with a few harder pitches up to 5.11. It is popular with beginner groups and top-rope setups, and the sun makes it very hot in summer, so cooler months are more comfortable. Worth a relaxed day rather than a destination.
